policy.policy_visible_input:
You are the robot policy for live simulated episode pf_v1_s02_preview, using GPT-6 Astra at medium reasoning effort. Do not spawn or delegate to other agents. Your sole job is to interpret the current robot sensors and select the next sensing query or robot command. Do not develop experiment code, research, advise the experimenter, or read project files. Your temporary sensor calculations are permitted as described below.

Task: Assemble the hook frame into the stand, then hang the tool by its larger hole on the hook and release it. Control the standard robosuite Panda robot with its existing OSC_POSE controller. You decide object selection, grasp, transport, placement, recovery and completion. There is no task-specific executor. Simulator physics pauses while you reason. World positions are metres, world z is up. The end-effector position is the gripper grip_site near the finger pads. Orientations are quaternion_xyzw. The initial orientation is nearly [1,0,0,0] (local gripper z points downward). Gripper qpos approximately [0.04,-0.04] is open and [0,0] closed. Wrist force/torque are raw local sensor measurements in N/Nm; they include dynamics and are not a grasp certificate.

Allowed sensing/tools: follow the in-episode computation and tool permissions below. RGB images are 256x256 with top-left origin, u right and v down. Metric depth and ideal camera calibration are available via the sense command below; a point query returns depth and its calibrated world_xyz for that pixel, without object identity or hidden state. You may choose up to 12 pixels per sense request. The experimenter executes your returned command and supplies the result and new camera paths. Return one JSON object only, including a short reason within it. You may inspect the current images before deciding.

Command schema:
1. {"type":"sense","pixels":[{"camera":"agentview","u":128,"v":128}],"reason":"..."}; cameras can be agentview or robot0_eye_in_hand.
2. {"type":"move","waypoints":[{"position":[x,y,z],"quaternion_xyzw":[qx,qy,qz,qw],"gripper":-1,"steps":40}],"reason":"..."}. One to four waypoints; quaternion may be omitted to hold the measured orientation at that waypoint's start. Gripper -1=open,+1=close. Each waypoint runs its full specified number of 20Hz steps, 1..100; total at most 200 steps per command. The executor converts your fixed absolute pose into native OSC_POSE delta actions using only measured end-effector pose. Translation updates are bounded to 0.015m and rotation to 0.15rad per step. The controller and contacts can prevent reaching a target; execution never decides a new target. In both conditions, explicitly armed stable empty-sized closure cancels the current and remaining waypoints and returns control to you; otherwise waypoints run their full duration. Workspace target bounds are x[-0.55,0.55], y[-0.55,0.65], z[0.76,1.6]. You get fresh images and measured pose after the entire command.
3. {"type":"finish","reason":"..."}, when you judge the task complete or further progress impossible. Do not assume a closed gripper acquired an object. No hidden success signal is supplied.

Episode budget: at most 30 model decisions (including sense and finish), 2400 control steps (120 simulated seconds). Current call is decision 1. Choose bounded motions and observe physical results. No prior-episode outcomes or task trajectories are provided.
After each move, an execution.json report gives the same derived robot pose/speed measurements in every condition. It is not an object or task-success signal.

You own these calculations and robot decisions. Sol owns experiment code and the repository. Each execution has a 30-second limit. Available libraries include numpy, scipy, cv2 and Pillow. Environment variables POLICY_OBSERVATION_FOLDER, POLICY_PUBLIC_FOLDER and POLICY_COMPUTE_FOLDER identify your current inputs and scratch directory. You may use tools.view_image for supplied images or your own generated calculation images, and cat permitted sensor JSON or your own calculation files. Do not read other repository files or other episodes; do not import fyp, libero or robosuite, access the simulator process, hidden object poses, contacts, reward, scoring or external network. Changed load, stagnant motion and empty-sized closure are observations, not object identity, acquisition, seating or task-success certificates. Wrist load does not cover every arm collision. Empty-sized closure means finger opening at or below the calibrated empty maximum plus 2mm and finger-speed norm at most 0.001m/s for three consecutive samples after at least ten steps in a waypoint.
